repository.name: common
repository.description: Go libraries shared across Prometheus components and libraries.

issue.body:
here https://github.com/prometheus/common/blob/098669c08af8eee3da33d1d4a4f242a5242cccb8/config/http_config.go#L781-L797

because the error is nil, we may/would be moving nils around, leading to nil pointer dereference

body:
Looking at the code, it may be because of https://github.com/prometheus/common/issues/790, so it may not be only related to `3.4.0`
I'll mark it as a bug, PRs to work on this are welcome.

Hey folks!

Did a quick dive into this crash and it looks like I've pinned down what triggers it.

---

### What actually blows up

* If your `tls_config` **has** `cert_file` + `key_file` but **no** `ca_file`, then `t.settings.CA` is **nil**.
* Because you're using file‑based secrets, Prometheus creates the *hot‑reload* `tlsRoundTripper`.
  ```go
	if tlsSettings.immutable() {
		// No need for a RoundTripper that reloads the files automatically.
		return newRT(tlsConfig)
	}
	return NewTLSRoundTripperWithContext(ctx, tlsConfig, tlsSettings, newRT)
  ```
* When the CA *hash* changes (because you rewrote `server.crt`) Prometheus tries to rebuild the `tls.Config`.
  ```go
	t.mtx.RLock()
	equal := bytes.Equal(caHash[:], t.hashCAData) &&
		bytes.Equal(certHash[:], t.hashCertData) &&
		bytes.Equal(keyHash[:], t.hashKeyData)
	rt := t.rt
	t.mtx.RUnlock()
	if equal {
		// The CA cert hasn't changed, use the existing RoundTripper.
		return rt.RoundTrip(req)
	}
  ```
* `updateRootCA` fails to parse the garbage PEM and returns **false**.
* The code then formats an error message and calls `t.settings.CA.Description()`, but because **no `ca_file` was ever configured, `t.settings.CA` is `nil`** — so we dereference a `nil` pointer and crash.
* Next scrape hits this code:

  ```go
  if !updateRootCA(...) {
      // here
      return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to use specified CA cert %s", t.settings.CA.Description())
  }
  ```

  <details>
  <summary>Boom:</summary>

  ```
    panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
    [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0xcc919e]

    goroutine 921 [running]:
    github.com/prometheus/common/config.(*tlsRoundTripper).RoundTrip(0xc000d200b0, 0xc0013523c0)
        /home/nd/develop/gopath/pkg/mod/github.com/prometheus/common@v0.63.0/config/http_config.go:1380 +0x9fe
    net/http.send(0xc0013523c0, {0x60dd760, 0xc000d200b0}, {0x0, 0x0, 0x0})
        /home/nd/go/src/net/http/client.go:259 +0x52a
    net/http.(*Client).send(0xc000a8edb0, 0xc0013523c0, {0x0, 0x0, 0x0})
        /home/nd/go/src/net/http/client.go:180 +0x15a
    net/http.(*Client).do(0xc000a8edb0, 0xc0013523c0)
        /home/nd/go/src/net/http/client.go:728 +0x13ef
    net/http.(*Client).Do(0xc000a8edb0, 0xc0013523c0)
        /home/nd/go/src/net/http/client.go:587 +0x49
    github.com/prometheus/prometheus/scrape.(*targetScraper).scrape(0xc000d00840, {0x6126290, 0xc000535d50})
        /home/nd/develop/github.com/ndk/prometheus/scrape/scrape.go:836 +0x35c
    github.com/prometheus/prometheus/scrape.(*scrapeLoop).scrapeAndReport(0xc0007c69a0, {0xc207e09b04e17d8a, 0x1c0b2b5a8, 0x8198920}, {0x501ae92, 0xedfd101fb, 0x8198920}, 0x0)
        /home/nd/develop/github.com/ndk/prometheus/scrape/scrape.go:1448 +0xb2d
    github.com/prometheus/prometheus/scrape.(*scrapeLoop).run(0xc0007c69a0, 0x0)
        /home/nd/develop/github.com/ndk/prometheus/scrape/scrape.go:1373 +0x50b
    created by github.com/prometheus/prometheus/scrape.(*scrapePool).sync in goroutine 920
        /home/nd/develop/github.com/ndk/prometheus/scrape/scrape.go:612 +0x12b8
  ```
  </details>

I'm guessing that's exactly what happened to the original reporter: Prometheus reloaded a partially‑written cert and keeled over.

---

### Quick repro

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: tls‑panic
    scheme: https
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["localhost:8443"]
    tls_config:
      cert_file: "server.crt"
      key_file:  "server.key"
```

```bash
# 1. Generate cert/key
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -days 3650 \
  -keyout server.key -out server.crt -subj "/CN=localhost"

# 2. Start Prometheus with the config above. Wait for the first scrape. You can get a self-signed certificate error, but it doesn't matter. We don't even need a working target.

# 3. Corrupt the cert so reload fails
printf '-----BEGIN GARBAGE-----\nabc\n-----END GARBAGE-----\n' > server.crt

# 4. Wait for the next scrape. Panic!
```

---

### Proposed fix

```diff
if !updateRootCA(tlsConfig, caData) {
-    return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to use specified CA cert %s", t.settings.CA.Description())
+    if t.settings.CA == nil {
+        return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to use specified CA cert: none configured")
+    }
+    return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to use specified CA cert %s", t.settings.CA.Description())
}
```

Makes Prometheus log an error instead of crashing.

I've got a patch + unit test ready - happy to PR if nobody's on it yet. :)

UPD: https://github.com/prometheus/common/pull/792
UPD2: I couldn't reproduce the exact call stack.
My best guess: the certs were rotated by changing the `cert_file`/`key_file` paths in the config and then reloading Prometheus via `SIGHUP` or `/-/reload`. The new scrape pool hit the same nil dereference on its very first scrape. Different trigger — same underlying bug.

repository.name: common

issue.body:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/16622#issuecomment-2935997383

Prevents a nil-pointer panic in `tlsRoundTripper` that occurred when cert_file/key_file were set but no ca_file, and the CA reload failed. The code now returns a descriptive error instead of crashing.

body:
> My best guess: the certs were rotated by changing the `cert_file`/`key_file` paths in the config and then reloading Prometheus.

In my setup, certs are reissued periodically (I don't think the key changes, although I could be wrong) but no signal is sent to Prometheus- it should pick up the new certs on it's own.

> > My best guess: the certs were rotated by changing the `cert_file`/`key_file` paths in the config and then reloading Prometheus.
> 
> In my setup, certs are reissued periodically (I don't think the key changes, although I could be wrong) but no signal is sent to Prometheus- it should pick up the new certs on it's own.

Could you share the `scrape_configs` section of your Prometheus configuration?

When you reissue the certificates, do you overwrite the same files in-place, or do you write to temporary files first and then atomically replace the originals?

How often does reissuance occur? On a predictable schedule, or at seemingly random intervals?

Here is one of about 15 scrape jobs that has TLS enabled. They all use the same key/cert/ca files
```
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: node
    scheme: https
    tls_config:
      cert_file: /pki/prometheus.crt
      key_file: /pki/prometheus.key
      ca_file: /pki/certs/root_ca.crt
    static_configs:
      - targets: <snip>
    relabel_configs: <snip>
    metric_relabel_configs: <snip>
```

Certificate (re)issueance is managed with `smallstep` `step-cli ca renew`: https://smallstep.com/docs/step-cli/reference/ca/renew/
They're valid for 24h, and looking at the logs it seems to renew them every ~15-16 hours:

> If the file does not exist, [...]; otherwise WriteFile truncates it before writing
